headline: FEMA's Tea-Nap Bunkers Rated: 'Adequate Recliners, But No Pre-Noon Waivers'
deck: As mass leaf-blight sweeps the nation, Americans are urged to embrace nap protocols and surge pricing.
article:
The leaf-blight crisis has pushed FEMA to scatter tea-nap bunkers through city centers. Reviewers award them a tepid 2.5 stars because the recliners sit well enough yet refuse any meeting before eleven. Portland evacuees mutter about lost productivity points while Seattle merchants slap surge prices on single-serve bags and cite the usual legal escape hatch.

Workers now face an official start time of 11:17 a.m. Mary Dorrington, an office refugee, sits in a narrow cot nursing lukewarm chamomile and wonders how recovery from missing Earl Grey became a scheduled event. Local HOA president Ted Manfield continues arguing for an earlier snooze, though only the bunker walls hear him.

The National Tea Association warns that leaf stocks are thinning fast, which may soon force afternoon singalongs on every remaining employee. The 11 a.m. workday culture looks increasingly fragile when tea itself threatens to vanish.
author: Blaine T. Teagarden, Senior Infrastructure Analyst

oped.title: Blaming Hats for the Blight: A Modest Proposal to Fine the Bareheaded
oped.author: Viscount Archibald Steepley, Founder of the Pre-Noon Waiver Denial Society and Majority Shareholder in Seattle's Last Decent Recliner Factory
oped.body: FEMA's Tea-Nap Bunkers supply the precise lumbar support a gentleman needs between eleven and noon. The blight itself arises not from any shortcoming among tea barons but from citizens' ridiculous hats, which evidently block the afternoon light required for proper steeping. Surge pricing on naps is sound policy; those unwilling to pay simply merit their exhaustion. I requested a pre-noon waiver last Tuesday to settle my yacht's tea menu and was correctly denied, confirming the system works. The remedy is to fine every headwear that fails my standards, with proceeds funding my new line of regulation bonnets. This spares the nation further upheaval while leaving my own timetable untouched.

classifieds.text: Blighted Seattle tea crates, 40% off before FEMA seizes them for bunker rations. Surge pricing starts at noon, cash only, no pre-11 inquiries.
Urgent: Nap technicians needed for Tea-Nap Bunkers, shifts begin 11am. Must ignore leaf-blight panic and enforce recliner etiquette, benefits include surge tea vouchers.
Blighted tea baron, 42, seeks desperate nap partner for post-11am bunker dates. No waivers, bring your own recliner and tolerance for afternoon pricing.
Apology from Midtown firm: We scheduled a 9:45 meeting amid the national nap protocol. Fines paid in surge tea, offering free bunker slots as penance.

stories.headline: Leaf Blight Hits Southern Tea Plantations, USDA Counts 47 Percent Drop in Early-Morning Yield
stories.deck: Growers now petition for noon waivers on harvest crews already delayed by federal rest mandates.
stories.article:
Blight has cleared 2.3 million acres in Georgia and the Carolinas, sparing only the afternoon flush. Surge-priced bales leave warehouses by 1 p.m., after which crews must halt under the new labor rules.

Extension agents hand out "Post-Meridian Hardy" seed packets with orders to sow only after the 11 a.m. siren. Earlier planting would breach the same statute blocking equipment deliveries.

stories.headline: Seattle Tea Barons Post Record Quarter After Nap-Bunker Contracts Reach $4.2 Billion
stories.deck: Firms are now bidding on exclusive rights to supply recliners that double as boardroom furniture after 11 a.m.
stories.article:
FEMA bunker mandates have let three Seattle firms lease every warehouse south of the Sound. Recliner shares climbed 19 percent once buyers learned each unit carries a tea warmer set for 10:58 a.m.

The nationwide ban on pre-noon meetings has crammed every client call into the 11:15 slot, creating sudden demand for portable brew kits that slide under conference tables.
